name: Wide-Area Vacuum
definition: A commercial dry vacuum explicitly identified by its manufacturer for wide-area or large-carpet cleaning, using a broad floor head, powered brush system and onboard dust collection in a push or ride/stand-on format.
includedScope: Broad push brush vacuums for large carpeted routes
Stand-on vacuums explicitly positioned as wide-area alternatives
excludedScope: Ordinary upright, canister and backpack vacuums without wide-area positioning
Carpet extractors and sweepers without vacuum filtration
Wet pickup and hazardous-dust applications unless specifically rated
headline: Wide-area vacuum types, carpet metrics, filtration and buyer checks
description: Technical reference for commercial wide-area vacuums covering push and stand-on formats, brush and filtration systems, representative models and route-based procurement verification.
metaDescription: Wide-area vacuum guide covering cleaning paths, brushes, filtration, representative models, carpet tests and buyer checks.
disclaimer: Independent category reference, not carpet-care, indoor-air, electrical, ergonomic or certification advice. Verify the exact regional model, carpet approval, filter and bag configuration, cable or battery and service parts.

keyFacts.label: Category boundary
keyFacts.value: Manufacturer wide-area positioning and system architecture take priority; no universal cleaning-width threshold defines the category.
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official product pages use the stated operating format and equipment architecture for the named machines.
keyFacts.scope: Named models and reviewed regional configurations; no universal dimensional threshold is inferred.

keyFacts.label: Primary work interface
keyFacts.value: Broad powered brush head, suction airflow and onboard bag or filter system.
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources document wide cleaning paths, powered brushes, vacuum motors and bag/filtration systems.
keyFacts.scope: Exact brush, pad, nozzle, floor and consumable configuration.

keyFacts.label: Productivity boundary
keyFacts.value: Manufacturer area rates are source-specific, not achieved-site guarantees
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific widths, speeds or stated productivity figures under their own reporting conventions.
keyFacts.scope: Named manufacturer figures only; no cross-brand normalization or ranking.

keyFacts.label: Configuration boundary
keyFacts.value: Width, brush setting, bag, filter, cable or battery and regional voltage are model-specific.
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official pages publish materially different configurations and reporting methods.
keyFacts.scope: Delivered product number, voltage, battery or cable, consumables and local service terms.

systemFlow.name: Brush contact
systemFlow.componentFamily: Powered roller brush and height setting
systemFlow.role: Agitates carpet pile and moves soil toward pickup.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document powered brushes and height adjustment.

systemFlow.name: Air pickup
systemFlow.componentFamily: Nozzle, airflow path and vacuum motors
systemFlow.role: Transports loosened dry soil into the collection system.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish model-specific motor and airflow data.
systemFlow.scope: Source methods and regional electrical configuration.

systemFlow.name: Separation and collection
systemFlow.role: Retains collected soil and conditions exhaust air.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources publish bag capacities and filtration options.
systemFlow.scope: Exact installed bag and filter part numbers.

systemFlow.name: Route operation
systemFlow.componentFamily: Handle or stand-on controls, cord or battery
systemFlow.role: Moves the cleaning head across the planned area.
systemFlow.evidence: Reviewed models include push corded and stand-on battery formats.
systemFlow.scope: Route, operator, cable management and battery duty.

variants.name: Push wide-area brush vacuum
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator walks behind and steers a broad head
variants.spaceConstraints: Turning, furniture, doors and cord routing can limit use
variants.limitations: Wide heads increase edge and detail work in congested areas.
variants.evidence: Kärcher, NSS, Truvox and Tornado explicitly label push models as wide-area vacuums.
variants.scope: Named models; no fixed width threshold.

variants.name: Heavy-duty broad upright
variants.taskScale: Large carpet areas with an upright-like chassis
variants.spaceConstraints: Weight and storage differ from conventional uprights
variants.limitations: A broad upright label is not universal wide-area equivalence.
variants.evidence: Nilfisk positions GU700A for daily cleaning of large carpet areas.
variants.scope: Named model and reviewed product number.

variants.name: Stand-on wide-area alternative
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator rides on a standing platform
variants.spaceConstraints: Turning, load, charging and operator training require review
variants.limitations: Stand-on architecture is not interchangeable with push units.
variants.evidence: Kärcher positions Chariot 3 CV 86/1 where a wide-area vacuum could be used.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning path
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Exact regional model and installed head
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Width alone does not establish pickup or achieved output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish widths from 64 to 86 cm for reviewed models.

performanceMetrics.name: Brush system and height
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Matches agitation to carpet pile and soil
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Brush geometry, speed and setting method vary
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Higher speed or more positions do not prove better cleaning.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers document counter-rotating, single-brush and adjustable systems.

performanceMetrics.name: Airflow, vacuum and motor data
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Describes parts of the pickup system
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Test points, units and electrical configurations differ
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not rank cross-brand cleaning from CFM, kPa or watts alone.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish different subsets of motor, airflow and vacuum data.

performanceMetrics.name: Bag and filtration
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports dust capacity and indoor-air planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Media, test method, seal and installed option must be known
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: HEPA or efficiency wording is not comparable without the complete system and test basis.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Nilfisk, NSS, Truvox and Tornado publish bag and filtration details.
performanceMetrics.scope: Exact installed parts and cited test claim.

performanceMetrics.name: Area productivity
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Obstacles, edge work, bag changes and cable moves reduce achieved output.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Selected official pages publish source-specific area rates.
performanceMetrics.scope: Source conditions only; no normalized ranking.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Achieved area per labor hour and pickup result
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Choosing by cleaning width or advertised ft²/h alone
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a timed route and repeatable soil trial.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Measure normal obstacles, edge work and consumable changes.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record passes, rework, bag state and brush setting.
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources publish model-specific widths and rates.

procurementDecisions.assessment: Specify part numbers and evidence for the delivered system.
procurementDecisions.basis: Reviewed models offer different standard and optional filtration.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Filter-media efficiency is not automatically whole-machine capture.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require the bag, filter and seal configuration in the quote.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Inspect bypass paths and replacement intervals.

procurementDecisions.assessment: Select the architecture after mapping the route and support process.
procurementDecisions.basis: Reviewed products include push corded and stand-on battery formats.

procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Check doors, turns, ramps, storage, charging and egress.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brush contact affects pickup, pile appearance, drive load and wear.

engineeringChecks.reason: Capacity and filtration claims depend on installed consumables and seals.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record every bag and filter part number.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official pages publish model-specific collection and filter options.

engineeringChecks.reason: Route length, outlet layout and charging change usable productivity.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Map outlets or charging and confirm regional electrical parts.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Reviewed products use different cord and battery systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Large heads and heavier bodies affect storage, stairs and maintenance.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Demonstrate transport and routine brush, bag and blockage access.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official dimensions and manuals show model-specific service architecture.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-69:2021
standards.applicability: Safety scope for wet and dry commercial vacuum cleaners, including power brush provisions; it is not a carpet-cleaning performance ranking.

standards.scope: Confirm regional adoption, dust class where relevant and exact product conformity.

standards.evidence: ASTM publishes the method title and scope.
